Subject: Signatory flow + Exhibit C (data residency) — initial intake

Hi team,

Attaching the initial Order Form + a draft Exhibit C that the buyer (SignalPath) included with their compliance packet. They raised two things I want legal to triage before we proceed to redlines:

1) Signatory flow: they have a regional signatory requirement — different signatories for EU/US entities. They asked if we can accept a multi-entity signature matrix or whether Redwood needs a single parent counterparty.

2) Exhibit C: their language wants EU data residency for logs and an access notice window of 90 days. We typically keep logs in multi-region by default with a 30-day access window for debug. Need guidance on acceptable alternative language and whether we should flag a Dedicated/private deployment requirement.

Quick asks:
- Kimberly: can you confirm if the Exhibit C language is a show-stopper or a negotiable scope?
- Jonas: if we accept multi-entity sign-off, what does that do to our signature authority map (do we need a delegated signatory)?
- Rishi: if this triggers a Dedicated/private requirement, what lead time estimate should we give the AE?

I copied Claire from SignalPath — they asked for a week turn. I'm OK with a 3–4 business day legal first pass.

Attachments: SignalPath_OrderForm_v1.xlsx, ExhibitC_DataResidency_draft.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Signatory flow + Exhibit C (data residency) — initial intake

Thanks for the context, Marissa — quick read. High-level response:

- Exhibit C (data residency): the buyer's draft is stricter than our standard template. Key asks we should consider: require logs to be stored in EU-only; 90-day access window; right to audit language. My initial position: EU-only residency for logs is negotiable for hosted customers where we can set region pinning, but we should avoid hardwriting "EU-only" unless they commit to Dedicated or Private deployment or we accept an exception with attendant commercial uplift and SLA. 90-day access window is longer than our standard 30 days; we can agree to 60 days with a data-processing addendum and fees.

- Signatory flow: multi-entity signature is acceptable operationally (we do this for several enterprise customers). We need to map the counterparty legal entity names to the Order Form and ensure at least one signature matches the invoicing/legal entity. If they want separate entity obligations, that complicates liability/indemnity and we should avoid fragmenting liability across entities.

Action items for legal first pass (I will take these):
1) Mark up Exhibit C to add alternative language (Option A: EU log residency with Dedicated; Option B: hosted + 60-day access + fee).
2) Add guidance notes on signatory matrix and recommend redline language requiring counterparty to confirm invoicing entity.
3) Flag indemnity/residency interplay for review by contracts team (Jonas).

I can get a redline back by EOD 2025-09-29 if no major follow-ups.

-Kimberly

Kimberly — thanks. Quick notes from contracts/ops perspective:

- If we allow a multi-entity signature matrix, we must require the Order Form to include a single "billing/legal entity" field that ties to the invoice and tax details. Otherwise collections and enforceability become messy. We should also require a contact with authority at each entity for notice.

- If we move to Dedicated or Private as part of residency commitment, procurement lead time is typically 6–8 weeks (infra + capacity + networking/SCIM/KMS setup). That should be presented as a separate line item in the mutual action plan (MAP) — buyer needs to accept lead time and cost uplift.

- Minor ask: can legal add a clause that expressly allows us to switch to a compatible model variant (i.e., fallback model) if the customer's deployment constraints change? We want to preserve our routing/fallback policies.

I'll coordinate with Rishi on the Dedicated timeline numbers once we confirm the acceptance criteria.

Jonas

Thanks Marissa / Kimberly / Jonas — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Couple points to close from our side:
- We can accept 60 days for access if Redwood confirms a clear SLA and the data will not leave EU storage unless we request (Documented exception).
- On signatories: SignalPath will provide a signature matrix; billing/legal entity will be SignalPath Holdings Inc (US) for initial PO but our product team requires a separate EU affiliate signatory for GDPR accountability.
- We are OK to include a procurement line in the MAP for Dedicated if needed; can you share estimated uplift numbers?

I've attached a cleaned version of the Order Form with our billing block filled and a proposed signature matrix (see attachments). We're aiming to have a countersigned Order Form within two weeks if the residency path is clarified.
